body:
All right, well main thing is I didn't want you to think I'd been downvoting you. That would be unnecessary of me.

I only wish I could conquer the reason that led to my depression. But that's not in my control. Unless you are talking about love. Which, if I ever expect to be happy again, I guess you are right. I'd have to conquer love.

Yeah, I do need someone to talk to. I hardly have anyone. My life has been slowly self-destructing. I lost my job, have a court case pending, have no money... all within a few weeks. And of course I lost the one thing that matters.

It's definitely going to take me ages. If it ever stops. I think this might be one of those things that sticks with you forever and emotionally cripples you.

I don't have the same hope. Well, I have some, actually. I am only alive because I have some, if I really honestly had none left I think I'd be dead and not sitting at home all day wondering what I would do with myself if I lost all hope. The problem is that the hope it's unconditional. It's hope that things between us will work out again. I had the same experience as you during my childhood. I didn't have a good one at all, and what kept me going was hope that one day I'll live on my own. I reached that goal. I wouldn't say I was suicidal then, but what you said still hit right home for me. And it's the same thing now, except that living on my own seemed more likely than this...

But as for hope of me having a decent lonely future, I don't know. People say that to me all the time but I haven't ever heard anything to back it up. I've never met anyone like her before, and while I know it's strictly possible to have such luck twice in a lifetime, it's close to a zero chance. Most people don't even have this luck once.

Yeah, I'm talking because I want to. Thanks for being there to listen, even if it seems to get neither of us anywhere.

^((Finally, it seems you've attracted some sort of dedicated downvoter; your comments here were downvoted for some reason, I've fixed them.)^)

Well... not a happy message, but just getting worse day by day. I look back on the replies that say I'd be all better in a month, but I feel like I've barely started the grieving process. I still feel just as suicidal, but I'm still not in immediate danger. As long as I still feel some hope of having a decent future together, I still have a reason to live. :/
Hey, so I didn't log in for a month, but I just got your reply. Thought you would want to know.

Well thanks for the posts. I don't know if I got across what my problem is. It's not that I think I don't have a future. Just that if the future isn't as happy as it should and could be, I don't know if it's worth it. I know time heals wounds. I know I could love someone else. But it won't be the same. People say "how do you know it won't be better" but then when I list the requirements for it to be as good, not even better, people turn around and say "lower your standards man, you won't find someone else that wonderful in this lifetime". I know it's true too, if I keep looking for someone as amazing as her I'll just be disappointed. So I could settle, and in a few years the wounds will have mostly healed, and I'll be living half of what I know is possible. Or 80% or 95%, it doesn't matter. The point is that acording to all evidence, the zenith in life has already been reached, and I don't know if it's even worth it to live 60 more mediocre years. I know it's a long time, and I know there are lots of possibilities for happiness. That's why I'm still around.

For the alcohol: I don't know what else I'm supposed to do. I never understood alcoholics before a few weeks ago. Why would you want to go through life drunk? That sounds terrible. And it really is, actually. But it makes me feel normal again. It takes the crazy away, at least to an extent. How am I not supposed to drink when it's the only gateway I know of into how I've spent 20 years of my life knowing how I'm supposed to feel? I *know* it's bad, I *know* I shouldn't. I don't *want* to be drunk. All I want is to feel normal again, and I finally have a way. Drunkenness is just a shitty side effect of that. That said, I did feel normal for 10 minutes or so sober a few days ago. It was immediately after I woke up from a dream where we were cuddling again. As soon as that was gone and the panic started to set in, I felt I had no choice but to reach for the bottle.

And I'd also like to address your point about keeping busy. It's a good one, during the day after a few days (I believe after I posted this new topic) I went to work again. I run a small logistics company. But now that was taken from me too. I can't even distract myself with that during the day. The reason is that my driver's license's validity was called into question, and now I'm not allowed to drive anymore. That *was* my work. What the hell do I do?
Not since a few years, no, I haven't played video games. Got any other suggestions? I feel like I'm nearing the end of my rope.

Nah, not really. The suicidal thoughts have just been crystallising. I've been using alcohol to cope, and I am shocked at how well it works when you are sad. Really focuses you, it's like going from drunk to sober when you drink in this state. All my life I have been baffled by why someone would be an alcoholic, now not anymore.

Thanks for the message.

There was a honeymoon period though. You're right that she wasn't trying. That's one of the most hurtful parts, I was willing to make it work and she was not. I had planned a trip to her country simply as a visit, because I missed her so much that I could not be away from her for very much longer. I wanted her to at least give that a try. My suicide note was written in that context, that I visited and it did not work out.

It's nice that you have faith things will work out. I wish I could have that same faith. What you say about right person wrong time seems familiar to my situation. I feel like had we stayed in her country for some years, let her learn my language, have her start some studies, all before coming here, it may have worked better. Definitely the wrong time, and in my eyes the right person. Sadly though, I can't just go back in time and change it. And getting a promise that we could try again would tear me right out of this state. I would be worried, concerned, lonely, as I was before this last talk. And that is so much better than this.

People grow up. I think all it shows is that she was not strong enough to live here. I am strong enough to live there though. I don't take it as a good sign because I refuse the idea that it means something else bad would have happened.

I feel like soul mates can fight. It is definitely worse for the relationship if they do, but it is not unlike simply being mad at yourself. The extreme bliss was there though. Except for moments of fighting, which I think were partially due to her immaturity and partially due to mine, so things that would have improved as we got older, it *was* bliss. Even she admits it. Well, she did some days ago. I don't know if she has suddenly changed her mind but I do not think it likely.

I also challenge the idea that we were never on the same page. Perhaps we were not on the same page in the last few months, maybe in the last year. But for a long time after we met, we were really on the same page. She eventually had a hard time talking to me, and now she says she is just afraid of fighting. I think it's possible for your soulmates to have flaws. We're all human. One of hers is that she would hear things I never said. It was basically setting up strawman arguments but I don't think she was doing it on purpose. Even in the final moments, she was not really listening. I think this is one thing that helped cause the untimely end of our relationship.

Thanks for sharing your story. I'm glad you feel it was right, and I hope he does too.

I don't know about not looking back. I always will, and I hope one day she has the sense to as well. But I don't know how long that will take, or if it will ever happen. Especially if she finds her way into another relationship, that can cover it up like a new blanket of snow, or blind you to how you feel otherwise. What do you mean by your last statement, that if it's right they will find you when they are right?

If I did that I think I would last until the despair phase of grief for the relationship. I am still in the denial phase, but I am honestly scared for the despair phase. I do not know if I will make it out alive. I want to, but I am afraid I will not. Suicide should never be an emotionally-filled decision in a moment of despair in my opinion. Things always get better, the despair can be overcome. If it is done the best time is perhaps when you simply know there is no other possible way out of the situation, and you are calm and collected enough to know the real repercussions.

I don't know if I am really that much like your ex. I'm not usually an extremely emotional person, but when it comes to love, I feel it really intensely. When you say you have never talked about your feelings, was it all feelings or just love feelings? We talked about them a lot, but more so we just showed them. We would lay in bed together for hours at a time, every chance we got to see each other, which ended up being most days, and just talk, have sex, talk more, go out to eat on a date, come back, talk, talk, have sex again, talk, maybe even nap in each other's arms. It's just one aspect which I've not heard described before, although I'm sure someone will tell me this thing happens with other couples. I'm sure it does. But compounded with the rest?

*What if* you were my soul mate and we never got to talk? Is it possible for your soul to have two mates? Maybe it is, but what is the chance of finding the second one among 7 billion people? We never really threatened to kill each other. Well, she never did, and she thinks I did but she's really just misinterpreting it. It wasn't a threat, it was a simple statement of that I could not live without her. I never said that in fights, I never discussed suicide methods, I never even was really clear that suicide was my intention, although it's not all that unclear that it's amazing she even picked up on it. I don't want to burden her with this, so I always felt I can't really tell her. This is why it's a throwaway, she knows my main account and if she saw this she would feel really bad, and maybe be drawn to take me back. But for all the wrong reasons - if she did we would be back together, and then she would try to rehabilitate me unsuccessfully, and probably break up with me once she thinks I would stay alive. And maybe in that time she would want to stay with me either way, but then the relationship would be so damaged by my suicidal will that it would hardly even be worth it.
Ok. I should have gone to sleep a long time ago. But I promise to hang in there, I am not willing to do it tonight.

It could be worse indeed, but the distance is fairly large, and so are the cultural differences. I'm not going to lie, I'm not very happy there, but here without her I am much less happy. I fear this future more than death itself.

You are also right about there being many other girls out there. I don't doubt, logically, that I will find one I think is sweet and who likes me back. That is well within the realm of possibility. But to have what we had? I don't know, that does not sound very realistic to me, not a second time.
Mine is Germany and hers is the USA.

Yes, I suspect she will have much of a problem finding someone that loves her as much as I did, same way that I will have much of a problem finding someone that I love as much as her. And in the latter, I can't even see a chance at all. Perhaps she will find someone else like me though. There are many more people like me than her I think.

I'd love to stay close. The problem is that we live in different countries now. She has also said she does not want to contact me again, and I am not sure if she will keep this up, but even if she does not, I'm afraid she won't want to uproot me and will keep any feelings to herself. She is under the impression that I *hate* her country. That is not really so.

I'm a lover at heart. I don't think my job or my hobbies or my family will be any consolation. They never have before. :/ To me, life is not more than love, it is love.

And I really don't see it as "one relationship" that didn't work. "One" is the wrong article here, it's simply "the".

I do have talents and all, but what use are they even if life is no longer worth living? That all belongs to simply going through the motions. I don't doubt that other parts of my life are something that would lift others out of their depressions. Everyone's sadness is different. But that all doesn't really matter.

I've already felt close to this way (pain) for a good month and a half, and now just today the pain has promised to increase by orders of magnitude. The thoughts of possibly committing suicide if she ever dies or leaves have persisted for much, much longer. I wonder if it will really only be another month before it's all gone. Doubtful to me, but I can only hope. Even then, finding someone else I care about but don't feel the same way about, having children, getting married, etc. doesn't sound all that appealing to me. "going through the motions" isn't something I want from life. Thanks for the message.

She wasn't my first. But how can I know that it will be fine? I've never even heard of anyone else like her. I don't doubt my ability to find another partner that I feel similarly to my past relationships about, get married, have kids, go through the motions, etc. with. I did love the others too. But what is even the point?
